page: OVHcloud c2-60 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, meaning hyperthreading is disabled with one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 60.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core, alongside 400 GB of local SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data places the instance in the average tier across most performance metrics. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is recorded at 1535.88, while multi-core performance reaches 24461.89. Memory bandwidth tests yield 1775.09 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 120.4 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For database and web operations, the server achieves 25.27 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a static web serving throughput of 16.25 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds are average for prompt processing but drop to weak or poor tiers for text generation tasks, particularly with larger models.

From a resource density perspective, the dedicated core allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio offer reliable performance without the CPU stealing risks associated with shared-core environments. This makes the instance highly suitable for compute-bound workloads such as web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. However, the lack of GPU acceleration and weaker text generation benchmarks make it less suitable for intensive machine learning or large-scale AI inference workloads.
